sounds.name: Pinged Filter Arpeggio

sounds.name: Ducking Spring Chords
sounds.ref: In the style of Huerco S. — “For Those of You Who Have Never (And Also Those Who Have)” (2016)

sounds.name: Blue Veils Ring Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of Delia Derbyshire — “Blue Veils and Golden Sands” (1967)
sounds.blurb: A hovering, glassy drone whose two inner tones slide slowly past each other in the springs.

sounds.name: Just Third Keys
sounds.ref: In the style of Hans-Joachim Roedelius — “Durch die Wüste” (1978)
sounds.blurb: A gentle keyboard tune where every key plays a sweet, perfectly still major third.
sounds.how: Two oscillators follow the keys together, Oscillator 2 tuned a just major third above Oscillator 1: the 5:4 ratio, 386 cents, rather than the equal-tempered 400. A just third does not beat, so every key sounds a dyad of unusual calm, something an equal-tempered keyboard cannot play. The keyboard is mono, but two oscillators on one key make a two-note chord.

sounds.name: Breathing Decay Arpeggio

sounds.name: Glowing Peak Arpeggio
sounds.ref: In the style of Philip Glass — “Opening”, Glassworks (1982)
sounds.blurb: Rolling triplet broken chords in A minor, some notes glowing brighter where they meet a fixed resonance.

The envelope shaper is dry on the left with a little spring on the right.

sounds.name: Northern Wasteland Arp
sounds.ref: In the style of Michael Hoenig — “Departure from the Northern Wasteland” (1978)
sounds.blurb: A soft sixteenth-note arpeggio, bright and dry on the left, dark and echoing on the right, the dry side slowly fading in and out.

Channel 1 takes it dry, its OUTPUT FILTER cutting a little bass so it sounds thin and close; channel 2 takes only the springs, its OUTPUT FILTER cutting the treble so the echo is dark and far. Oscillator 3’s slow triangle in channel 1’s level column (O6) fades the dry side in and out every seven seconds, so the arpeggio steps forward and sinks back into its own echo.

sounds.name: Birdsong in the Springs
sounds.ref: In the style of Beaver & Krause — “In a Wild Sanctuary” (1970)

Oscillator 3’s slow square is pinned into the decay column (L5); every few seconds it doubles and then halves the decays, so the bird switches between quick runs and slower calls.

sounds.name: Seven-Key Zither
sounds.ref: In the style of Laraaji — “Day of Radiance” (1980)
sounds.blurb: Bright, hammered zither cascades in a seven-note scale that divides the octave evenly, ringing in the springs.
sounds.how: INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 sets how far each key moves the oscillators. Turned up from 5 to 8.57, every key is 1.71 semitones, so seven keys span an exact octave: an equal seven-note scale, close to Thai and some gamelan tunings, that sits between the keys of a piano. A ramp and narrow pulse go through a filter the trapezoid plucks, and the spring rings on the left like the open strings of a zither.

- INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 8.6 · 1.7 semitones per key: seven keys make an octave.
- Filter FREQUENCY 6.3 · 601 Hz, RESPONSE 4 · low-pass, LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

sounds.name: Shakuhachi Breath
sounds.ref: In the style of Hozan Yamamoto — “Silver World” (1971)
sounds.blurb: A breathy bamboo flute, half air and half tone, with a slow head-shake vibrato and a bend under the stick.
sounds.how: A shakuhachi is as much breath as note, so noise and Oscillator 2’s triangle go into the filter together and come out as one breathy tone; COLOUR sets how airy the breath is. A soft envelope swells each note in the way a player blows into the edge. Oscillator 3 adds yuri, the slow, wide head-shake vibrato, and the joystick’s horizontal row is pinned to Oscillator 2’s pitch so the stick can bend a note down, the meri a player makes by dipping the chin.

sounds.name: Andean Pan Pipes
sounds.ref: In the style of Los Kjarkas — “Llorando se fue” (1981)
sounds.blurb: Hollow, chuffing pan-pipe notes in a quick huayno rhythm, each one blown with a puff of air.

sounds.name: Highland Pipes and Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of Gordon Duncan — “Just for Seumas” (1994)
sounds.blurb: A nasal pipe chanter playing a march with sharp grace notes, over a reedy drone that never stops.
sounds.how: The two output channels carry the two halves of a bagpipe. Channel 1 is the chanter: Oscillator 1’s ramp through a nasal filter peak and a fast envelope, played from the keys, and the grace notes are just very short high notes before each melody note. Channel 2 is the drone: Oscillator 2, its triangle leaned into a ramp, tuned to A two octaves down and pinned straight to column C, past the envelope shaper, so it sounds steadily whatever the keys do.

sounds.name: Trapezoid Horn Call
sounds.ref: In the style of Dennis Brain — Mozart’s Horn Concertos (1953)
sounds.blurb: A round, mellow French horn playing a hunting call in six-eight, each note opening brighter as it is blown.

The trapezoid on row 11 is pinned into the filter frequency (N11) as well as shaping the level, so as the envelope rises the filter opens with it and the note blooms from dark to bright, then darkens as it fades: the brass opening a fixed synth needs a second envelope for. sounds.name: Harmon Mute Trumpet
sounds.ref: In the style of Miles Davis — “’Round About Midnight” (1957)
sounds.blurb: A thin, buzzing, intimate muted trumpet with a small blat on each note and a late shiver of vibrato.

sounds.name: Shower-Scene Stabs
sounds.ref: In the style of Bernard Herrmann — “Psycho” (1960)
sounds.blurb: Shrieking, sliding high-string stabs that repeat by themselves for as long as a key is held.
sounds.how: The stabs are the envelope repeating on its own: OFF below 6 starts it again after a short rest, so one held key is a volley of downbows. The trapezoid on row 11 is also pinned into both oscillators’ pitch (I11 and J11), so every stab starts a few semitones sharp and slides down as it decays: the shriek. Two ramps slightly out of tune with each other give the harsh, massed-violin edge.

sounds.name: Noise Snare and Ghosts
sounds.ref: In the style of Cybotron — “Clear” (1983)
sounds.blurb: A crisp electronic snare on the backbeat, with lower ghost notes skittering round it.

Oscillator 2’s triangle is the skin, dipped by the trapezoid (J11); noise through a bright filter is the wires. Both go into the envelope shaper together, and the keys tune the skin, so the low ghost notes sound like softer hits nearer the rim.

- Listen for: short, dull blips through the Default patch’s quick envelope.

sounds.name: Rhythm Box Hi-Hats

sounds.name: Fluttering Handclaps
sounds.ref: In the style of Shannon — “Let the Music Play” (1983)
sounds.blurb: Electronic handclaps on the backbeat, each a quick flutter of several hands, with a pickup roll at the end of the bar.

A burst of band-limited noise through the envelope is one hand; to make several, Oscillator 3’s square at about 30 Hz is pinned into both output level columns (O5 and P5). With the OUTPUT LEVEL knobs just past half way, the square switches both channels on and off, chopping every burst into a flutter. Oscillator 3 runs free, so no two claps flutter quite the same.

sounds.name: Tabla Teental
sounds.ref: In the style of Zakir Hussain — “Making Music” (1987)
sounds.blurb: A sixteen-beat teental cycle of ringing, pitched tabla strokes, with the bass drum’s glide on the stick.

The joystick’s vertical row is pinned to Oscillator 1’s pitch, so the stick is the heel of the hand pressing the bayan to make its sliding ge.

sounds.name: Mikrophonie Tam-Tam

sounds.name: Skaro City Hum
sounds.ref: In the style of Tristram Cary — “The Daleks” (Doctor Who, 1963)

sounds.how: Two low oscillators a couple of semitones apart are multiplied in the ring modulator, so neither pitch survives: only their sum and their slow difference, which beats like a machine turning over. Oscillator 3 is then run at audio rate, about 40 Hz, into Oscillator 1’s frequency column: frequency modulation from an oscillator the VCS3 usually keeps for slow sweeps, which turns the hum into a grinding roar. No key is pinned to a pitch; the keyboard only opens the envelope.

sounds.name: Robot Intonation
sounds.ref: In the style of Bruce Haack — “The Electric Lucifer” (1970)
sounds.blurb: A buzzing machine voice chattering in syllables, its vowels flipping and its pitch rising and falling like speech.
sounds.how: Oscillator 2’s narrow pulse is the larynx, a buzz full of harmonics, and a resonant filter picks out one band of them as a vowel. Oscillator 3’s square, at about three times a second, flips the filter between two vowels, and the envelope, left cycling on its own, chops the buzz into syllables. INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 is turned right down, so the keys no longer play a scale: a fifth on the keys moves the voice only two semitones, the small rise and fall of a voice talking.

sounds.name: Time-Ship Wheeze
sounds.ref: In the style of Brian Hodgson — the TARDIS take-off, “Doctor Who” (1963)
sounds.blurb: A heaving, grinding wheeze that rises and falls over and over while the springs swell and draw back with it.
sounds.how: Noise through a filter set close to ringing gives a pitched rush of air. One slow Oscillator 3 triangle, leaned into a ramp, does two jobs at once: pinned into the filter frequency it heaves the pitch of the rush up and down, and pinned into the reverb MIX column it makes the springs swell wetter on each heave and draw back drier between. sounds.name: Dying Circuits
sounds.ref: In the style of Louis and Bebe Barron — “Forbidden Planet” (1956)
sounds.blurb: A whistling circuit that swoops and chirps on its own, its tone tangling with a second voice it is feeding.
sounds.how: The Barrons built circuits that screamed and died as they overloaded. Here the filter sings its own sine, and Oscillator 1’s ramp also goes through it; then the filter’s output is pinned back into Oscillator 1’s frequency column, at audio rate. Each now modulates the other: the filter bends the oscillator, the bent oscillator changes what the filter rings with, and the loop chirps and gargles. The envelope cycles on its own, and its trapezoid sweeps the filter up each time, so the circuit seems to strain and give out.

- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

sounds.name: Red-Alert Whoop
sounds.ref: In the style of Dick Mills — the BBC Radiophonic Workshop’s “Doctor Who” alarms (1970s)
sounds.blurb: A whooping siren on the left and a pulsing low klaxon on the right, sounding together as one alarm.
sounds.how: The two output channels carry two different sounds. Channel 1 is the siren: Oscillator 1’s ramp through a nasal filter, its pitch pushed up over and over by Oscillator 3 leaned into a ramp, so each whoop rises and snaps back. Channel 2 is the klaxon: Oscillator 2’s square pinned straight to column C, with Oscillator 3’s square pinned into channel 2’s level column, so the amplifier opens and shuts in time with the whoops. One slow oscillator clocks both halves of the alarm.

sounds.name: Deep-Sea Sonar

sounds.blurb: A dark rotor roar chopped nine times a second into the thud of helicopter blades.
sounds.how: Dark noise and a very low ramp through the filter are the engine and the air. The chop is in the output amplifiers: both OUTPUT LEVEL knobs are turned down almost shut, and Oscillator 3’s pulse is pinned into both level columns, so the amplifiers themselves open and slam shut nine times a second. The stick’s horizontal row on Oscillator 3’s frequency spins the blades up or down.

steps.title: Engine and air
steps.why:
Dark noise and Oscillator 1’s low ramp into the filter.
- Pins H7 and H2. Unpin D2 and I8.
- Noise LEVEL 7 · 0.7 V, Noise COLOUR 3.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 4.2 · 40 Hz, ramp LEVEL 5 · 0.5 V.
- Filter FREQUENCY 5.5 · 327 Hz, RESPONSE 2 · low-pass, LEVEL 8 · 1.3 V.
- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: It approaches
steps.why:
The filter through a slow, held envelope to both outputs.
- Pins D10, B12 and C12.
- Envelope ATTACK 10 · 1.0 s, ON 10 · 2.5 s, DECAY 9 · 6.4 s, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 7 · 1.2 V.
- Listen for: a dark roar that rises and holds.

steps.title: Chopped in the amplifiers
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s pulse into both output level columns (O5, P5), with both OUTPUT LEVEL knobs nearly shut.
- Pins O5 and P5.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 6.2 · 9.13 Hz: about nine times a second. square LEVEL 7 · 1 V, SHAPE 3: short open, long shut.
- OUTPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 5.5 · 10% open, OUTPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 2 at 5.5 · 10% open.
- Listen for: the roar chopped into the thud-thud-thud of rotor blades.

steps.title: Spin up, spin down
steps.why:
The stick’s horizontal row into Oscillator 3’s frequency (K15).
- Pin K15.
- RANGE (horizontal) 4 · ±0.8 V: left spins the blades faster, right slows them.
- Listen for: nothing new until you move the stick.

sounds.name: Thunder in the Springs
sounds.ref: In the style of Tod Dockstader — “Apocalypse” (1961)
sounds.blurb: A crack of noise slams the spring reverb and rolls away into a long, booming rumble.
sounds.how: The VCS3’s spring unit sounds best abused. A loud, short burst of dark noise strikes it hard, with MIX nearly all spring, and the springs answer with a crash and a long boom. Both output filters cut the treble, so the boom rolls like distant thunder, and Oscillator 3, slowly, moves the MIX so the rumble seems to roll and return.

steps.title: A crack of noise into the springs
steps.why:
Dark noise through a short envelope into the reverb, and the reverb to both channels.
- Pins D7, G12, B14 and C14. Unpin D2, B12, C12 and I8.
- Noise LEVEL 7 · 0.7 V, Noise COLOUR 3.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 0 · 0 ms, DECAY 5.5 · 320 ms, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 7 · 1.2 V.
- Reverb MIX 8.5 · 81% spring: nearly all spring. Reverb LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: a crack slamming the springs and a long, rattling boom after it.

steps.title: Far away
steps.why:
Both output filters turned to cut the treble.
- OUTPUT FILTER CHANNEL 1 at 2.5 · treble cut, OUTPUT FILTER CHANNEL 2 at 2.5 · treble cut.
- Listen for: the crack softening into a deep rumble.

steps.title: Rolling
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s slow triangle into the reverb MIX (M6).
- Pin M6.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 4.5 · 1.64 Hz, triangle LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: the rumble rolling away and back.

context.rev.mix: In this sound: how much of the strike is boom. Lower and the crack itself comes through.
context.env.decay: In this sound: the length of the crack.
context.noise.colour: In this sound: higher for a sharp, near crack, lower for a heavy, far one.

tweaks.hear: A sharp, close lightning crack.
The left side bright and rattling, the right still far away.

sounds.name: Dripsody Drops
sounds.ref: In the style of Hugh Le Caine — “Dripsody” (1955)
sounds.blurb: Clean, pitched water drops, each a quick plink that bends down and trails off in a cave.
sounds.how: The filter is the drop: RESPONSE high makes it sing a sine, and the keys are pinned into its frequency so each key gives a different drop. A short envelope plinks it, and the trapezoid does two jobs: pinned into the filter frequency it bends each drop down as it dies, and pinned into the envelope’s own decay column it shortens the decay while the envelope is high and lengthens it as it falls, so each drop snaps at the top and trails off slowly.

steps.title: A singing filter on the keys
steps.why:
The filter rings on its own; the keys move its frequency (N8), and a trace of noise starts it at once.
- Pins H7 and N8. Unpin D2 and I8.
- Filter FREQUENCY 6.5 · 699 Hz, RESPONSE 7 · oscillating, LEVEL 5 · 0.5 V.
- Noise LEVEL 1.5 · 0.03 V, Noise COLOUR 5.
- INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 3 · 0.6 semitones per key: about an octave of filter for an octave of keys.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: Plink
steps.why:
The filter through a short envelope to both outputs.
- Pins D10, B12 and C12.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 0 · 0 ms, DECAY 4.5 · 140 ms, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 8 · 1.6 V.
- Listen for: clean, short sine plinks on each key.

steps.title: The drop bends
steps.why:
The trapezoid into the filter frequency (N11): each plink starts high and sinks as it dies.
- Pin N11.
- TRAPEZOID LEVEL 4 · 0.5 V.
- Listen for: each plink bending down: a drip.

steps.title: The trapezoid times its own fall
steps.why:
The trapezoid into the envelope’s decay column (L11) as well: a short decay at the top, a long one near the bottom.
- Pin L11.
- TRAPEZOID LEVEL, already set, sets how uneven the fall is.
- Listen for: a quicker snap at the top of each drop and a longer, softer tail.

steps.title: A cave
steps.why:
The envelope shaper into the reverb, and the reverb to both channels in its place.
- Pins G12, B14 and C14. Unpin B12 and C12.
- Reverb MIX 5 · 48% spring, LEVEL 8 · 1.3 V.
- Listen for: drops falling in a dripping cave.

context.env.trapLevel: In this sound: two things at once, how far each drop bends and how unevenly it dies.
context.in.ch1: In this sound: the spread of the drops across the keys.
context.env.decay: In this sound: the size of the drop.

Duller, woodier taps, more like a marimba.

sounds.name: Night Crickets
sounds.ref: In the style of Luc Ferrari — “Presque rien no. 1” (1970)
sounds.blurb: A cricket trilling on the left and small waves washing on the right, a beach at night.
sounds.how: The two output channels are two parts of the scene. The cricket on channel 1 is Oscillator 1’s high sine cut into a fast trill by the envelope, which, with OFF low, cycles on its own about fifteen times a second. The sea on channel 2 is noise through the filter, pinned straight to column C past the envelope, and Oscillator 3, very slowly, opens and closes the filter so the wash surges and pulls back.

steps.title: A cricket, left
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s high sine through the envelope shaper to channel 1 only, the envelope cycling fast on its own.
- Pins D1 and B12. Unpin D2, C12 and I8.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 8.7 · 4.3 kHz, sine LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 3: about 4 kHz, a little edged.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 0 · 0 ms, DECAY 2.5 · 25 ms, Envelope OFF 1.5 · repeats, off 47 ms: a trill. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 8 · 1.6 V. PAN CHANNEL 1 at 2 · left of centre.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: a high, fast trill on the left.

steps.title: The sea, right
steps.why:
Dark noise through the filter straight to channel 2 (C10).
- Pins H7 and C10.
- Noise LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, Noise COLOUR 3.
- Filter FREQUENCY 5.5 · 327 Hz, RESPONSE 1 · low-pass, LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- PAN CHANNEL 2 at 8 · right of centre.
- Listen for: a dark, steady wash on the right.

steps.title: Small waves
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s very slow triangle into the filter frequency (N6).
- Pin N6.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 3.2 · 0.43 Hz: one wave every two or three seconds. triangle LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 7.
- Listen for: the wash surging up and pulling back.

context.osc1.freq: In this sound: the cricket’s size. Lower is a fat cicada.

A buzzing cicada.

sounds.name: Slowed Bird Calls
sounds.ref: In the style of Basil Kirchin — “Worlds Within Worlds” (1971)
sounds.blurb: Low, hooting calls that rise and sink as they sound, warbling like birdsong slowed to a quarter speed.
sounds.how: Kirchin slowed recordings of birds until their calls became huge, strange voices. Oscillator 1’s sine, folded a little for a reedy edge, plays the calls from the keys. Oscillator 3’s triangle, about six times a second, is the warble a slowed bird keeps, and the trapezoid, pinned into Oscillator 1’s frequency too, lifts each call as it begins and lets it sag as it ends. Deep in the springs it sounds like a forest at the wrong speed.

steps.title: A hooting call
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s sine through the envelope shaper to both outputs, following the keys.
- Pins D1, I8, B12 and C12. Unpin D2.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 6 · 262 Hz, sine LEVEL 7 · 0.7 V, SHAPE 6.5. INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 5 · 1 semitone per key.
- Envelope ATTACK 6 · 83 ms, ON 3 · 220 ms, DECAY 7 · 1.2 s, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: a plain, reedy hoot on each key.

steps.title: A slowed warble
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s triangle into Oscillator 1’s frequency (I6).
- Pin I6.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 6 · 7.81 Hz: about six times a second. triangle LEVEL 2.5 · 0.09 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: a throaty warble through each call.

steps.title: The call rises and sags
steps.why:
The trapezoid into Oscillator 1’s frequency (I11).
- Pin I11.
- TRAPEZOID LEVEL 3 · 0.3 V.
- Listen for: each call swooping up as it starts and sagging as it ends.

steps.title: A forest at the wrong speed
steps.why:
The envelope shaper into the reverb, and the reverb to both channels in its place.
- Pins G12, B14 and C14. Unpin B12 and C12.
- Reverb MIX 6 · 57% spring, LEVEL 8 · 1.3 V.
- Listen for: the calls hanging in a deep, ringing space.

context.osc1.shape: In this sound: the reedy edge of the call.

sounds.name: River over Stones
sounds.ref: In the style of Annea Lockwood — “A Sound Map of the Hudson River” (1989)
sounds.blurb: Water bubbling and gurgling over stones on the left, the rush of the river behind it on the right.
sounds.how: The filter is used here not as a sound but as a source of random voltages: noise through it at about 60 Hz leaves a slow, wandering voltage, and that is pinned into the frequency columns of Oscillators 1 and 2, whose sines jump and slide at random like water over stones. Their tones go through the envelope to channel 1. Channel 2 takes the noise itself, past the envelope and darkened by the output filter, as the river’s rush.

steps.title: Random voltages from noise
steps.why:
Noise into the filter, its frequency so low that only a slow, wandering voltage comes out.
- Pin H7. Unpin D2, C12 and I8.
- Noise LEVEL 10 · 1.5 V, Noise COLOUR 2.
- Filter FREQUENCY 3.3 · 61 Hz, RESPONSE 3 · low-pass, LEVEL 10 · 2 V.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: Bubbles, left
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s sine and Oscillator 2’s triangle through the envelope shaper to channel 1, and the random voltage into both their frequencies (I10, J10).
- Pins D1, D4, I10, J10 and B12.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 7.2 · 911 Hz, sine LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 5.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 6.8 · 601 Hz, triangle LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 5.
- Envelope ATTACK 6 · 83 ms, ON 10 · 2.5 s, DECAY 8 · 2.7 s, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V. PAN CHANNEL 1 at 2 · left of centre.
- Listen for: two tones bubbling and gurgling at random on the left.

steps.title: The rush, right
steps.why:
The noise straight to channel 2 (C7), darkened and turned down.
- Pin C7.
- OUTPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 2 at 6 · 20% open, OUTPUT FILTER CHANNEL 2 at 2.5 · treble cut, PAN CHANNEL 2 at 8 · right of centre.
- Listen for: a soft rush of water on the right.

context.vcf.freq: In this sound: how fast the water moves. Higher is a quick trickle, lower a slow, deep pool.
context.vcf.level: In this sound: how far the bubbles jump.
context.out2.level: In this sound: how loud the river behind the bubbles is.

tweaks.hear: A fast, chattering brook.
Deeper, glugging water.

sounds.name: Ear Tones
sounds.ref: In the style of Maryanne Amacher — “Sound Characters (Making the Third Ear)” (1999)
sounds.blurb: Two piercing high tones, one in each ear, and between them a low phantom tone that slides slowly.
sounds.how: Amacher wrote for tones the ear makes itself. Two high tones about 170 Hz apart, one on each output channel, make the inner ear produce their difference as a low third tone that neither speaker plays; on speakers they also beat. Oscillator 2 sounds steadily on channel 2, pinned straight to column C. Oscillator 1 swells in through the envelope on channel 1. Oscillator 3, very slowly, moves Oscillator 2, so the phantom tone glides.

steps.title: A high tone, right
steps.why:
Oscillator 2’s triangle straight to channel 2 (C4).
- Pin C4. Unpin D2, C12 and I8.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 7.9 · 1.9 kHz: about 1.9 kHz. Oscillator 2 triangle LEVEL 5 · 0.4 V, SHAPE 5. PAN CHANNEL 2 at 10 · right.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: a steady, piercing high tone on the right.

steps.title: Its partner, left
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s sine through a slow envelope to channel 1 only.
- Pins D1 and B12.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 8 · 2.1 kHz: about 2.1 kHz. Oscillator 1 sine LEVEL 5 · 0.4 V, SHAPE 5.
- Envelope ATTACK 10 · 1.0 s, ON 10 · 2.5 s, DECAY 9 · 6.4 s, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V. PAN CHANNEL 1 at 0 · left.
- Listen for: a second tone swelling in on the left, and between them a low, buzzing third tone.

steps.title: The phantom glides
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s very slow triangle into Oscillator 2’s frequency (J6).
- Pin J6.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 1.5 · 0.07 Hz, triangle LEVEL 3 · 0.1 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: the low phantom tone sliding slowly up and down.

context.osc2.freq: In this sound: the gap between the two tones, which is the pitch of the phantom.
context.out1.pan: In this sound: keep the two tones apart, one in each ear, for the effect on headphones.
context.osc3.tri: In this sound: how far the phantom glides.

Both tones in one ear: plain beating instead of a phantom.

sounds.name: Adnos Feedback Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of Éliane Radigue — “Adnos I” (1974)
sounds.blurb: A low, slowly beating drone whose overtones gather and shift as its own reverb tail feeds back into it.
sounds.how: Radigue built her drones from feedback, and the VCS3 can feed back inside itself. Two low tones a hair apart go through the filter into the reverb; the reverb’s output goes on to the envelope and the outputs, and is also pinned back into the filter’s input. The springs’ tail comes round again and again, at a low gain, so it thickens the drone without taking it over (turned up, the loop overloads and chokes itself silent), and Oscillator 3, very slowly, tilts the filter so different overtones come forward.

steps.title: Two low tones
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s sine and Oscillator 2’s triangle, a hair apart, into the filter.
- Pins H1 and H4. Unpin D2 and I8.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 4.8 · 73 Hz, sine LEVEL 7 · 0.7 V, SHAPE 4.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 4.8 · 74 Hz, triangle LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 5.
- Filter FREQUENCY 5.5 · 327 Hz, RESPONSE 4 · low-pass, LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: Through the springs to a slow envelope
steps.why:
The filter into the reverb (G10), the reverb into the envelope shaper (D14), and the envelope to both outputs.
- Pins G10, D14, B12 and C12.
- Reverb MIX 8 · 76% spring: mostly spring. Reverb LEVEL 3.5 · 0.2 V: low, because this is also the loop’s gain.
- Envelope ATTACK 10 · 1.0 s, ON 10 · 2.5 s, DECAY 9.5 · 9.8 s, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 10 · 2.5 V: full, to make up for it.
- Listen for: a low, beating drone swelling in from a distance.

steps.title: The tail fed back
steps.why:
The reverb’s output back into the filter’s input (H14).
- Pin H14.
- Reverb LEVEL, already set, is also the loop’s gain. Kept low, the tail adds to the drone; turned up, the loop overloads and chokes the drone away.
- Listen for: the drone thickening as overtones gather and smear.

steps.title: The light changes
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s very slow triangle into the filter frequency (N6).
- Pin N6.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 1 · 0.04 Hz, triangle LEVEL 3 · 0.1 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: different overtones coming slowly forward and sinking back.

context.rev.level: In this sound: the level out and the gain of the loop at once.
context.osc2.freq: In this sound: the speed of the slow beating.
context.vcf.response: In this sound: how much the loop sings at the filter’s frequency.

tweaks.hear: The loop overloading: the drone swells, then chokes itself away to silence within a few seconds.
A quicker, restless beating.

sounds.name: Scraped Feedback
sounds.ref: In the style of AMM — “AMMMusic” (1967)
sounds.blurb: A scraping, rasping howl made by a loop between two modules, its grain steered by one hand.
sounds.how: The ring modulator and the filter are pinned in a circle: the filter’s output goes into ring input B, Oscillator 2’s pulse into ring input A, and the ring modulator’s output back into the filter. The filter sings on its own, so the loop always has something in it; each pass multiplies it by the pulse and rings it again, and the result scrapes and howls. The stick’s horizontal row is pinned into Oscillator 2’s frequency and the filter frequency together, one gesture changing the whole loop.

steps.title: A singing filter
steps.why:
The filter rings on its own; a trace of noise starts it at once.
- Pin H7. Unpin D2 and I8.
- Filter FREQUENCY 6.6 · 754 Hz, RESPONSE 6.8 · oscillating, LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V.
- Noise LEVEL 3 · 0.1 V, Noise COLOUR 5.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: A circle through the ring modulator
steps.why:
Oscillator 2’s pulse into ring input A (E3), the filter into ring input B (F10), and the ring modulator back into the filter (H13).
- Pins E3, F10 and H13.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 6.3 · 357 Hz, square LEVEL 7 · 1 V, SHAPE 7.
- Ring modulator LEVEL 7.5 · ×3: the loop’s gain.
- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: Hear the loop
steps.why:
The filter through a slow, held envelope to both outputs.
- Pins D10, B12 and C12.
- Envelope ATTACK 6 · 83 ms, ON 10 · 2.5 s, DECAY 8 · 2.7 s, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 7 · 1.2 V.
- Listen for: a scraping, rasping howl: the loop between filter and ring modulator.

steps.title: One hand on the loop
steps.why:
The stick’s horizontal row into Oscillator 2’s frequency (J15) and the filter frequency (N15), and the stick pushed a little right.
- Pins J15 and N15.
- RANGE (horizontal) 4 · ±0.8 V, Joystick (left-right) 0.3 · +30%.
- Listen for: the scrape changing grain as the stick moves; sweep it slowly for the sound of bowed metal.

context.ring.level: In this sound: how hard the loop drives itself.
context.joy.x: In this sound: the improviser’s hand, moving the pulse and the filter together.

sounds.name: Three-Way Cross-Modulation
sounds.ref: In the style of Musica Elettronica Viva — “Spacecraft” (1967)
sounds.blurb: A buzz that goes metallic, then breaks into a chattering warble as three oscillators modulate each other in a ring.
sounds.how: The three oscillators are pinned in a circle: Oscillator 1’s sine into Oscillator 2’s frequency, Oscillator 2’s triangle into Oscillator 3’s frequency, and Oscillator 3’s triangle into Oscillator 1’s frequency. Each bends the next, which bends the next, which comes back round to the first, so a change anywhere runs all the way round. Only Oscillator 2’s square is heard, through the filter; the rest is all control.

steps.title: A plain buzz
steps.why:
Oscillator 2’s square into the filter, and the filter through a held envelope to both outputs.
- Pins H3, D10, B12 and C12. Unpin D2 and I8.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 6 · 262 Hz, square LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V, SHAPE 5.
- Filter FREQUENCY 7 · 1.0 kHz, RESPONSE 3 · low-pass, LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Envelope ATTACK 4 · 24 ms, ON 10 · 2.5 s, DECAY 7 · 1.2 s, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: a plain, buzzing square.

steps.title: One into two
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s sine into Oscillator 2’s frequency (J1).
- Pin J1.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 5.2 · 114 Hz, sine LEVEL 4 · 0.2 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: the buzz going metallic and clangorous.

steps.title: Two into three into one
steps.why:
Oscillator 2’s triangle into Oscillator 3’s frequency (K4), and Oscillator 3’s triangle into Oscillator 1’s frequency (I6). The circle is closed.
- Pins K4 and I6.
- Oscillator 2 triangle LEVEL 3 · 0.1 V.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 6.5 · 13 Hz, triangle LEVEL 4 · 0.2 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: the clang breaking into a chattering, tumbling warble.

context.osc1.sine: In this sound: how metallic the buzz is.
context.osc3.freq: In this sound: the speed of the chatter.

sounds.name: Persepolis Glissandi
sounds.ref: In the style of Iannis Xenakis — “Persepolis” (1971)
sounds.blurb: A harsh, dense mass that swells and screams upward in a huge glissando, then slides down and ebbs, again and again.
sounds.how: Two oscillators and bright noise make a dense, harsh mass. The envelope cycles on its own, with long attack and decay, and its trapezoid is pinned into three columns at once, both oscillators’ frequencies and the filter frequency: the whole mass slides up three octaves as it swells and back down as it ebbs, the massed glissandi Xenakis wrote. The spring adds the roar of a large space.

steps.title: A dense mass
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s ramp, Oscillator 2’s pulse and bright noise into the filter.
- Pins H2, H3 and H7. Unpin D2 and I8.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 5 · 92 Hz, ramp LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 4.4 · 50 Hz, square LEVEL 5 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 2.
- Noise LEVEL 4 · 0.2 V, Noise COLOUR 7.
- Filter FREQUENCY 7.5 · 1.5 kHz, RESPONSE 2.5 · low-pass, LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Listen for: nothing yet: row 10 is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: Swelling and ebbing
steps.why:
The filter through the envelope shaper to both outputs, repeating on its own.
- Pins D10, B12 and C12.
- Envelope ATTACK 10 · 1.0 s, ON 5 · 630 ms, DECAY 8.5 · 4.2 s, Envelope OFF 3 · repeats, off 220 ms. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V.
- Listen for: a harsh mass that swells and ebbs on its own.

steps.title: Glissandi
steps.why:
The trapezoid into Oscillator 1’s frequency (I11), Oscillator 2’s (J11) and the filter frequency (N11).
- Pins I11, J11 and N11.
- TRAPEZOID LEVEL 6 · 1.1 V: three octaves of slide.
- Listen for: the whole mass screaming upward as it swells and sliding down as it ebbs.

steps.title: A large space
steps.why:
The envelope shaper into the reverb, and the reverb to both channels in its place.
- Pins G12, B14 and C14. Unpin B12 and C12.
- Reverb MIX 5 · 48% spring, LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Listen for: the glissandi roaring in a hall.

sounds.name: Breathing Pulse Gesture
sounds.ref: In the style of Morton Subotnick — “Silver Apples of the Moon” (1967)
sounds.blurb: A stream of ringing ticks that speeds up and slows down, rising and falling in pitch, as if the patch were breathing.
sounds.how: The envelope cycles on its own and pings a ringing filter. The trapezoid is pinned into its own decay column, so each decay starts fast and slows as it falls: a sharp tick with a lingering, wah-like tail. Then Oscillator 3’s slow ramp is pinned into the decay column and into Oscillator 1’s frequency: as it rises the ticks lengthen and slow and the pitch sinks, as it falls they quicken and climb, the arching gestures Subotnick drew from his patches. The keys still set the pitch around which it all moves.

steps.title: Pinged, on its own
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s ramp into a ringing filter, through a short repeating envelope to both outputs; the keys play Oscillator 1.
- Pins H2, I8, D10, B12 and C12. Unpin D2.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 6.5 · 440 Hz, ramp LEVEL 5 · 0.5 V. INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 5 · 1 semitone per key.
- Filter FREQUENCY 6.5 · 699 Hz, RESPONSE 5.5 · sharp peak, LEVEL 9 · 1.6 V.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 0 · 0 ms, DECAY 4 · 91 ms, Envelope OFF 1.5 · repeats, off 47 ms. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 8 · 1.6 V.
- Listen for: quick, even pulses repeating on their own.

steps.title: The trapezoid shapes its own decay
steps.why:
The trapezoid into the envelope’s decay column (L11).
- Pin L11.
- TRAPEZOID LEVEL 5 · 0.8 V: the decay fast at the top and slow at the bottom.
- Listen for: each pulse now a sharp tick with a lingering tail.

steps.title: Breathing
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s slow ramp into the decay column (L6) and Oscillator 1’s frequency (I6).
- Pins L6 and I6.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 3.5 · 0.58 Hz: a breath every two seconds. triangle LEVEL 5 · 0.4 V, SHAPE 8: a slow rise and a quick fall.
- Listen for: the ticks slowing and sinking, then rushing and climbing: a gesture that breathes.

context.osc3.tri: In this sound: how far the gesture swings, in speed and pitch together.

sounds.name: Oscillations Throb
sounds.ref: In the style of Silver Apples — “Oscillations” (1968)
sounds.blurb: A twangy melody on the left over a buzzing drone on the right that throbs in quick, even beats.
sounds.how: Simeon’s oscillators played drones and pulses under the tune. The two output channels split the band: channel 1 is the melody, Oscillator 1 through a nasal filter and the envelope, from the keys; channel 2 is a drone, Oscillator 2 pinned straight to column C, never stopping. Oscillator 3’s square, in time with the riff, is pinned into channel 2’s level column with OUTPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 2 almost shut, so the drone throbs in eighth notes.

steps.title: The melody, left
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s ramp into a nasal filter and through the envelope to channel 1, following the keys.
- Pins H2, I8, D10 and B12. Unpin D2 and C12.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 6 · 262 Hz, ramp LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V. INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 5 · 1 semitone per key.
- Filter FREQUENCY 7 · 1.0 kHz, RESPONSE 4 · low-pass, LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Envelope ATTACK 1 · 4 ms, ON 3 · 220 ms, DECAY 5 · 210 ms, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V. PAN CHANNEL 1 at 2 · left of centre.
- Listen for: a twangy, nasal melody on the left.

steps.title: The drone, right
steps.why:
Oscillator 2’s square straight to channel 2 (C3).
- Pin C3.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 4.8 · 73 Hz: a low D. Oscillator 2 square LEVEL 5 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 6. PAN CHANNEL 2 at 8 · right of centre.
- Listen for: a buzzing drone on the right that never stops.

steps.title: The throb
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s square into channel 2’s level (P5), with OUTPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 2 nearly shut.
- Pin P5.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 5.5 · 4.65 Hz: eighth notes at the riff’s tempo. square LEVEL 7 · 1 V, SHAPE 5.
- OUTPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 2 at 5.5 · 10% open.
- Listen for: the drone pulsing in quick, even beats, a drum machine made of oscillators.

context.osc3.freq: In this sound: the throb’s tempo. Tune it to the riff by ear.
context.osc2.freq: In this sound: the drone’s note, under the tune’s key.
context.out2.level: In this sound: nearly shut, so the throb is all on and off. Higher and the drone sounds between beats.

tweaks.hear: Short, ticking pulses instead of even throbs.
A drone that swells on the beat instead of stopping between.

sounds.name: Ring-Mod Fuzz Freak-Out
sounds.ref: In the style of The United States of America — “The American Metaphysical Circus” (1968)
sounds.blurb: A snarling, clangorous fuzz lead that bends and opens wildly as the stick moves.
sounds.how: Both oscillators follow the keys a fifth apart and are multiplied in the ring modulator; through the filter, with Oscillator 1’s own ramp under it, the result is a snarling fuzz that still tracks the tune. The stick’s horizontal row is pinned into Oscillator 2’s frequency and the filter frequency together: one push detunes the fifth into clangour and opens the filter, the freak-out of a band that ran its whole sound through ring modulators.

steps.title: A fifth, multiplied
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s ramp into ring input A and Oscillator 2’s square a fifth up into ring input B, both following the keys.
- Pins E2, F3, I8 and J8. Unpin D2.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 6 · 262 Hz, ramp LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 6.4 · 392 Hz: a fifth up. Oscillator 2 square LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V, SHAPE 5.
- INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 5 · 1 semitone per key. Ring modulator LEVEL 5 · ×1.3.
- Listen for: nothing yet: the ring modulator is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: Fuzz
steps.why:
The ring modulator and Oscillator 1’s ramp into the filter, and the filter through the envelope to both outputs.
- Pins H13, H2, D10, B12 and C12.
- Filter FREQUENCY 7.2 · 1.2 kHz, RESPONSE 4.5 · sharp peak, LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 4 · 400 ms, DECAY 5.5 · 320 ms, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V.
- Listen for: a snarling, clangorous fuzz lead.

steps.title: A wobble
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s triangle into Oscillator 1’s frequency (I6), and so against Oscillator 2.
- Pin I6.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 5.6 · 5.15 Hz, triangle LEVEL 1.3 · 0.03 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: the fuzz shimmering and churning on long notes.

steps.title: Freak out on the stick
steps.why:
The stick’s horizontal row into Oscillator 2’s frequency (J15) and the filter frequency (N15).
- Pins J15 and N15.
- RANGE (horizontal) 3 · ±0.6 V: left detunes the fifth upward and opens the filter at once.
- Listen for: nothing new until you move the stick: then the fifth smears into clangour as the filter tears open.

context.joy.x: In this sound: the freak-out, detune and filter in one hand.

tweaks.hear: A sour, bell-like clang on every note.
A wah-like squeal on top of the fuzz.

sounds.name: Squealing Filter FM
sounds.ref: In the style of Allen Ravenstine — Pere Ubu, “The Modern Dance” (1978)
sounds.blurb: Nasal notes that sizzle and squeal, each one diving from a shriek as it dies.
sounds.how: Oscillator 3 is run at audio rate, about 180 Hz, into the filter’s frequency column, so the filter’s peak is swept back and forth faster than the ear can follow and throws off squealing, sizzling sidebands. The trapezoid is pinned into Oscillator 3’s own frequency: Oscillator 3 shoots up while the envelope is up and sinks as it decays, so every note dives from a shriek to a growl, the noises Ravenstine threw across a rock band.

steps.title: A ringing tone
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s ramp into a ringing filter and through the envelope to both outputs, following the keys.
- Pins H2, I8, D10, B12 and C12. Unpin D2.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 5.5 · 156 Hz, ramp LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V. INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 5 · 1 semitone per key.
- Filter FREQUENCY 7 · 1.0 kHz, RESPONSE 5.5 · sharp peak, LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 2 · 100 ms, DECAY 6 · 500 ms, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V.
- Listen for: a nasal, ringing tone.

steps.title: Oscillator 3 shakes the filter
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s triangle into the filter frequency (N6), at audio rate.
- Pin N6.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 9 · 177 Hz, triangle LEVEL 5 · 0.4 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: the tone squealing and sizzling.

steps.title: Every note dives
steps.why:
The trapezoid into Oscillator 3’s frequency (K11).
- Pin K11.
- TRAPEZOID LEVEL 4 · 0.5 V.
- Listen for: each note diving from a shriek into a growl as it dies.

context.osc3.freq: In this sound: where the dive lands. Lower and it ends in a rattle.

A piercing, whistling shriek.

sounds.name: Pulse Demon Wall
sounds.ref: In the style of Merzbow — “Pulse Demon” (1996)
sounds.blurb: A harsh wall of shredded, screaming noise that seizes up into feedback and pulses like an engine.
sounds.how: Noise is multiplied by Oscillator 2’s pulse in the ring modulator and rung through a filter close to oscillation. Then two outputs are fed back in: the filter’s output into Oscillator 2’s frequency, so the oscillator shredding the noise is itself shredded, and the envelope shaper’s output, row 12, the very signal going to the speakers, into the filter frequency. Oscillator 3’s pulse in both output level columns chops the wall into a pulse.

steps.title: Shredded noise
steps.why:
Noise into ring input A, Oscillator 2’s pulse into ring input B, the ring modulator into a ringing filter, and the filter through the envelope to both outputs.
- Pins E7, F3, H13, D10, B12 and C12. Unpin D2 and I8.
- Noise LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, Noise COLOUR 7.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 7 · 740 Hz, square LEVEL 7 · 1 V, SHAPE 8. Ring modulator LEVEL 8 · ×3.4.
- Filter FREQUENCY 7.5 · 1.5 kHz, RESPONSE 6.5 · sharp peak, LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 10 · 2.5 s, DECAY 7 · 1.2 s, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 6 · 0.9 V.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: a harsh, ringing roar of shredded noise.

steps.title: The filter shreds the shredder
steps.why:
The filter’s output into Oscillator 2’s frequency (J10).
- Pin J10.
- Filter LEVEL, already set, is how hard it pushes.
- Listen for: the roar seizing up into screaming, jittering feedback.

steps.title: The output comes back in
steps.why:
The envelope shaper’s output, row 12, into the filter frequency (N12) as well as to the speakers.
- Pin N12.
- Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL, already set, is now also the depth of the loop.
- Listen for: the wall tearing at itself, louder parts bending the filter.

steps.title: Pulse
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s pulse into both output level columns (O5, P5), with both OUTPUT LEVEL knobs nearly shut.
- Pins O5 and P5.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 5.8 · 6.35 Hz: about six times a second. square LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V, SHAPE 5.
- OUTPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 6 · 20% open, OUTPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 2 at 6 · 20% open.
- Listen for: the wall chopped into a pounding pulse.

sounds.name: Metal Machine Clank
sounds.ref: In the style of SPK — “Leichenschrei” (1982)
sounds.blurb: Clanging, inharmonic metal hits repeating on their own in a lurching long-short rhythm, slammed into the springs.
sounds.how: Oscillator 1’s folded sine times Oscillator 2’s pulse in the ring modulator gives an inharmonic clang like struck sheet metal, and a little noise adds the scrape. The envelope repeats on its own, and Oscillator 3’s slow square, pinned into the decay column, makes alternate groups of hits long and short, so the machine lurches. The hits go into the springs with MIX past half, hard enough to rattle them.

steps.title: Struck metal
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s sine into ring input A and Oscillator 2’s pulse into ring input B; the ring modulator and noise into the envelope shaper.
- Pins E1, F3, D13 and D7. Unpin D2, B12, C12 and I8.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 6.8 · 601 Hz, sine LEVEL 8 · 1 V, SHAPE 7.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 5.4 · 145 Hz, square LEVEL 7 · 1 V, SHAPE 6. Ring modulator LEVEL 6 · ×1.9.
- Noise LEVEL 3 · 0.1 V, Noise COLOUR 6.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: nothing yet: the envelope shaper is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: A machine that hits on its own
steps.why:
The envelope shaper, repeating, into the reverb, and the reverb to both channels.
- Pins G12, B14 and C14.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 0 · 0 ms, DECAY 5 · 210 ms, Envelope OFF 3.5 · repeats, off 380 ms. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 7 · 1.2 V.
- Reverb MIX 6 · 57% spring, LEVEL 8 · 1.3 V.
- Listen for: clanging metal hits repeating on their own, rattling the springs.

steps.title: A lurch
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s slow square into the envelope’s decay column (L5).
- Pin L5.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 3.8 · 0.79 Hz, square LEVEL 5 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 5.
- Listen for: groups of long, ringing hits and groups of short, quick ones: the machine lurching.

context.osc2.freq: In this sound: the metal. Small moves change the clang completely.
context.env.off: In this sound: the pace of the machine.
context.rev.mix: In this sound: how hard the springs are thrown about.

tweaks.hear: A higher, tinnier clank, like a scaffold pole.
A crashing, hall-sized machine.

sounds.name: Sine Data Clicks
sounds.ref: In the style of Ryoji Ikeda — “+/−” (1996)
sounds.blurb: Tiny, piercing high pips on the left and a dry click train on the right, ticking in a stuttering, data-like pattern.
sounds.how: Two channels, two kinds of tick. Channel 1: Oscillator 1’s very high sine and Oscillator 2’s low triangle through the shortest envelope there is, cycling on its own, so each cycle is a pip a hundredth of a second long. Channel 2: Oscillator 3’s pulse pinned straight to an output, where each edge is a click. The same pulse is pinned into the decay column, so the pips alternate short and long, and the long ones let the low triangle’s thump through.

steps.title: Pips, left
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s high sine and Oscillator 2’s low triangle through the shortest repeating envelope to channel 1 only.
- Pins D1, D4 and B12. Unpin D2, C12 and I8.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 9.3 · 8.1 kHz: about 8 kHz. Oscillator 1 sine LEVEL 6 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 5.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 4.4 · 50 Hz: about 50 Hz. Oscillator 2 triangle LEVEL 7 · 0.7 V, SHAPE 5.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 0 · 0 ms, DECAY 1.5 · 11 ms, Envelope OFF 2.5 · repeats, off 130 ms. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 8 · 1.6 V. PAN CHANNEL 1 at 3 · left of centre.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: tiny, piercing pips ticking on the left.

steps.title: A click train, right
steps.why:
Oscillator 3’s pulse straight to channel 2 (C5): each edge clicks.
- Pin C5.
- Oscillator 3 FREQUENCY 6.4 · 12 Hz: about twelve cycles a second. square LEVEL 5 · 0.5 V, SHAPE 2. PAN CHANNEL 2 at 7 · right of centre.
- Listen for: a dry, buzzing click train on the right.

steps.title: Stutter
steps.why:
The same pulse into the envelope’s decay column (L5): short pips and long ones in turn.
- Pin L5.
- Oscillator 3 square LEVEL, already set, sets how different they are.
- Listen for: the pips stuttering, the longer ones with a low thump inside.

context.env.decay: In this sound: the length of a pip. Any longer and it becomes a tone.
context.osc3.freq: In this sound: the rate of the clicks and of the stutter.
context.osc1.freq: In this sound: the pitch of the pips, near the top of hearing.

tweaks.hear: A dense, buzzing stream of pips.
An even, metronomic tick.

sounds.name: Reverse Tape Swell
sounds.ref: In the style of Ron Geesin — “As He Stands” (1973)
sounds.blurb: Each note sucked in backwards out of its own echo, swelling from nothing and stopping dead, like tape played in reverse.
sounds.how: The usual order is turned round: the sound goes into the reverb first, nearly all spring, and the reverb’s output goes into the envelope shaper. The envelope has a long attack and almost no decay, so each note’s echo swells up out of nothing and then cuts off, the shape of a reversed tape. The stick’s vertical row on both oscillators’ frequencies is a varispeed: push it and the whole sound slides like tape slowing and speeding.

steps.title: A tone into the springs
steps.why:
Oscillator 1’s ramp and Oscillator 2’s square an octave down into the filter, and the filter into the reverb (G10). Both oscillators follow the keys.
- Pins H2, H3, I8, J8 and G10. Unpin D2.
- Oscillator 1 FREQUENCY 6 · 262 Hz, ramp LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V.
- Oscillator 2 FREQUENCY 5.3 · 131 Hz, square LEVEL 4 · 0.3 V, SHAPE 5. INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 5 · 1 semitone per key.
- Filter FREQUENCY 7 · 1.0 kHz, RESPONSE 2 · low-pass, LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Reverb MIX 8 · 76% spring: nearly all spring. Reverb LEVEL 7 · 1 V.
- Listen for: nothing yet: the reverb is not pinned anywhere.

steps.title: The echo, backwards
steps.why:
The reverb into the envelope shaper (D14), and the envelope to both outputs.
- Pins D14, B12 and C12.
- Envelope ATTACK 10 · 1.0 s, ON 4 · 400 ms, DECAY 1 · 7 ms, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key: a slow rise and a sudden stop. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 7 · 1.2 V.
- Listen for: each note swelling out of nothing and stopping dead, like tape played backwards.

steps.title: Varispeed
steps.why:
The stick’s vertical row into both oscillators’ frequencies (I16, J16).
- Pins I16 and J16.
- RANGE (vertical) 4 · ±0.8 V: down raises both, up lowers both, by several semitones.
- Listen for: nothing new until you move the stick: then the whole sound slides, a tape slowing and speeding.

context.env.attack: In this sound: how long each backwards swell takes.
context.rev.mix: In this sound: how much of the swell is echo. Lower and it is just a slow fade-in.
context.joy.y: In this sound: the tape speed.

tweaks.hear: Swells that fall away softly instead of stopping dead.
A plain swell with only a little spring.

sounds.name: Struck Resonances
sounds.ref: In the style of Bernard Parmegiani — “De Natura Sonorum” (1975)
sounds.blurb: Knocks that ring at pitches the keys choose, bloom in the springs and ring on like struck metal as their tails feed back.
sounds.how: A short burst of noise from the envelope strikes a filter set just short of oscillation, which rings at a pitch: the keys are pinned into the filter frequency, so each key is a different resonance. The filter goes into the reverb, and the reverb’s output comes back into the filter’s input as well as to the outputs, so each strike’s tail is rung by the filter again and lingers, the struck-object resonances of Parmegiani’s tape pieces.

steps.title: A knock that rings
steps.why:
Noise through a very short envelope into the filter (H12), the keys on the filter frequency (N8), and the filter to both outputs.
- Pins D7, H12, N8, B10 and C10. Unpin D2, B12, C12 and I8.
- Noise LEVEL 9 · 1.2 V, Noise COLOUR 6.
- Envelope ATTACK 0 · 2 ms, ON 0 · 0 ms, DECAY 3 · 39 ms, Envelope OFF 10 · manual: waits for a key. Envelope SIGNAL LEVEL 10 · 2.5 V.
- Filter FREQUENCY 7 · 1.0 kHz, RESPONSE 5.5 · sharp peak, LEVEL 6 · 0.7 V. INPUT LEVEL CHANNEL 1 at 3 · 0.6 semitones per key.
- Oscillator 1 ramp LEVEL 0 · 0 V: the Default patch’s sawtooth is not used.
- Listen for: a knock that rings at a pitch the keys choose.

steps.title: Into the springs
steps.why:
The filter into the reverb (G10), and the reverb to both channels in its place.
- Pins G10, B14 and C14. Unpin B10 and C10.
- Reverb MIX 5 · 48% spring, LEVEL 5 · 0.5 V: no higher, because it will also be the loop’s gain.
- Listen for: each knock blooming in the springs.

steps.title: The tail is struck again
steps.why:
The reverb’s output back into the filter’s input (H14).
- Pin H14.
- Reverb LEVEL, already set, is also the loop’s gain: a little higher and the loop rings on by itself without being struck.
- Listen for: each strike ringing on like struck metal and smearing into the next.

context.vcf.response: In this sound: how long the knock rings. Past 6.6 it sings on its own.
context.in.ch1: In this sound: how far apart the keys’ resonances are.
context.rev.level: In this sound: the level, and the feedback of the tail into the filter.

tweaks.hear: Dry, woody knocks.
Soft, padded thuds that ring low.
